newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo stocks seen lacking clear direction.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo stocks seen lacking clear direction.

text.p: Tokyo stocks are likely to hunt for direction on Wednesday with interest focusing on individual issues, brokers said. As it is the first day of trade for June delivery, dealer activity should pick up and turnover will probably increase, they said.
On Tuesday, the 225-share Nikkei average lost 153.61 points or 0.77 percent to finish at 19,889.89. Its June futures fell 290 points to 19,860.
"There is a fair amount of profit-taking above the 20,000 threshold and gains are likely to be capped," said Kunihiro Hatae, Tokyo Securities general manager.

The cancellation of a planned merger between toymaker Bandai Co Ltd and Sega Enterprises Ltd, known for its Sega Saturn 32-bit videogame player, was not expected to have a big impact on the stock market, brokers said.
But they said the announcement, made late on Tuesday evening, could depress their shares, Sega's especially.

"The two firms will not be able to become Japan's Disney as they had initially hoped," a broker at a middle-sized brokerage said. "Shares of the firm that was going to be the survivor in the merger, Sega, will probably be under more selling pressure than Bandai."
Shares of Fujitsu Ltd added 10 yen to stand at 1,390. Fujitsu was the fourth most heavily traded issue on the Tokyo bourse at 2.57 million shares.
Tokyo Electron Ltd hit a high for the calendar year before retracing to 5,150 yen, up 100, by midday.

"The outlook for the firm's business is not exceptionally strong, but investors think that there is room for growth as the outlook for chip makers is improving," a broker at a medium-sized brokerage said.
NTT stood at 1.08 million yen, up 30,000. Earlier, it hit 1.1 million yen, a high for 1997.

"There hasn't been much fresh news to stoke buying but the issue is still being powered by the company's inclusion in the Morgan Stanley Capital International's Japan index," one broker said. "Once such large issues start moving, market activity in general could pick up and the market is following NTT closely."
Robust group earnings boosted Nissan Motor Co Ltd. It ranked second on the list of heavily traded issues and rose 46 yen to 785 in a turnover of 4.15 million shares.
The after-effects of a decision by Sega Enterprises Ltd and Bandai Co Ltd to cancel plans to merge were limited to the two firms.
Sega, known for its 32-bit videogame player, rose 80 yen to stand at 3,780, while Bandai lost 160 yen or 5.93 percent to 2,600 to become the third largest percentage loser.
"In the process leading up to the merger cancellation, there were media reports of discord within Bandai, and this has not been appreciated by the market," one fund manager said.

Speculation had been rife prior to the announcement of the cancellation, announced late on Tuesday, that the merger could be delayed due to strong opposition from mid-level managers at Bandai, a toymaker whose earnings have been buoyed by its recent runaway hit, the Tamagotchi virtual pet toy.
